items.title: docs: explain --n-cpu-moe with multiple GPUs in multi-gpu.md
items.body:
## Overview
--n-cpu-moe N keeps unloads experts on the CPU experts weights of the first n layers . Yes, its documented, but on multiple GPUs it confuses users, because the freed memory ends up on GPU0, but the last GPU runs out of memory.
- 3 issues about same problem  **#15136, #15263, #16579**
- in docs/multi-gpu.md about  --n-cpu-moe is not mentioned.
- this PR adds recipe how rebalance with **-ts** or -**ot**,the note about the KV cache of hybrid models, an example with measurements. 

## Additional information

 build b10603, 2 × RTX 5060 Ti, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q5_K_M, 262k context, 4 slots

items.title: llama : hybrid MoE expert cache with profile prefilling and zero-upload inference

labels.name: ggml
labels.description: changes relating to the ggml tensor library for machine learning

items.body:
## Overview

This PR adds hybrid MoE expert execution to `--cpu-moe` and `--moe-cache-mib`:
1. `--moe-cache-profile <file.strp>`: Pre-populates the GPU expert cache using offline-profiled routing distributions so the hottest experts start resident in VRAM.
2. `--moe-cache-hybrid`: Keeps profiled hot experts on the GPU while the CPU computes the remaining misses directly from host RAM in parallel. Misses do not wait for PCIe uploads during generation.
3. `--moe-cache-audit <file.jsonl>`: Provides a structured JSONL audit trail recording cache hit rates, resident expert IDs, and transfer overhead per generation.

## When to use it

The hybrid mode is for MoE models that do not fit in VRAM. It helps most when the GPU can hold only a small part of the experts: the CPU then computes many experts every token, and the hybrid runs that work in parallel with the GPU instead of after it. The further the model is beyond the VRAM, the more it gains; when most of the model fits, upstream's default offload (`-fit`) is faster.

| Situation | Machine, model, cache | Best upstream | PR hybrid + adaptive |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model much larger than VRAM | RTX 4060 Laptop 8 GB, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q6_K (27 GB), 4 GB cache | 22.5 t/s (`-fit`) | **37.7 t/s (1.7x)** |
| Cache holds a minority of the experts | L4, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B IQ4_XS (18.7 GB), experts kept in host RAM, cache capped at 5000 MiB | 33.5 t/s (cache, same cap) | **45.9 t/s (1.4x)** |
| Cache holds most of the experts the generation uses | L4 24 GB, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q6_K (27 GB), 16 GB cache, 1024 tokens | 51.6 t/s (`-fit`), 50.5 (cache) | 50.1 t/s |
| | L4 24 GB, Qwen3-Coder-Next UD-IQ4_XS (36 GB), 16 GB cache, 1024 tokens | 46.6 t/s (cache) | 42.6 t/s |
| Model fits, or nearly fits, in VRAM | L4 24 GB, Flint UD-Q4_K_XL (24 GB), 5800 MiB cache | 59.7 t/s (`-fit`) | 29.9 t/s* |
| | L4 24 GB, GLM-4.7-Flash Q8_0 (30 GB), 16 GB cache | 34.0 t/s (`-fit`) | 24.9 t/s* |

256 generated tokens unless noted. The laptop row is from the laptop tables below; the L4 rows are from Google Colab (12 vCPUs). \* measured before the faster cache fill described below.

Not every case is covered yet: on a 12 GB RTX 4070 SUPER a tester in this thread measured the reverse for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B IQ4_XS (upstream cache 101 t/s, hybrid 85, before the faster fill), which has not been re-measured.

## Additional information

- Tested against all 56 supported MoE architectures in `test-llama-archs`: all pass with 0 failures.
- End-to-end benchmark on RTX 4060 Laptop GPU: `llama-completion` achieves 0 bytes uploaded over PCIe during generation with 100% profile cache hits.
- Implements CUDA mailbox kernel synchronization in `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mailbox.cu` for coordinating asynchronous CPU/GPU token routing without stalls.
- Behavior change for existing `--moe-cache-mib` users (without the hybrid flags): the expert biases of the cached host layers (e.g. gpt-oss) are now copied to the GPU, and their size counts against the `--moe-cache-mib` budget, so the same value holds slightly fewer expert slots than on master. Models without expert biases are unaffected.

## Benchmarks (vs. upstream llama.cpp)

Generation speed with the MoE experts in host RAM and attention on the GPU.

**Hardware:** RTX 4060 Laptop (8 GB), 16 threads (8 used), 88 GB RAM. CUDA 13.4.
**Setup:** `llama-completion`, `-c 2048 -n 256 --temp 0 -s 1`, same 63-token prompt for every run, `--moe-cache-mib 4096` where a cache is used.
**Builds:** upstream = ggml-org/llama.cpp master `1b29621`; PR = this branch merged with that same master.
**No expert profile (`--moe-cache-profile`) was used.** `--moe-cache-adaptive` starts with an empty cache and fills it while generating.

### Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q6_K (mean of 2 rounds)

| Build | Flags | Generation t/s |
|---|---|---|
| upstream | (none; `-fit` chooses the offload) | 22.5 |
| upstream | `-ngl 99 --cpu-moe` | 19.6 |
| upstream | `-ngl 99 --cpu-moe --moe-cache-mib 4096` | 21.1 |
| PR | `-ngl 99 --cpu-moe --moe-cache-mib 4096` | 21.1 |
| **PR** | `... --moe-cache-hybrid --moe-cache-adaptive` | **37.7** |

### Qwen3-Coder-Next Q6_K (1 round)

| Build | Flags | Generation t/s |
|---|---|---|
| upstream | (none; `-fit` chooses the offload) | 18.0 |
| upstream | `-ngl 99 --cpu-moe` | 17.3 |
| upstream | `-ngl 99 --cpu-moe --moe-cache-mib 4096` | 15.4 |
| PR | `-ngl 99 --cpu-moe --moe-cache-mib 4096` | 15.4 |
| **PR** | `... --moe-cache-hybrid --moe-cache-adaptive` | **30.9** |

Hybrid-adaptive is about 1.7x the best upstream configuration on both models.

### Notes

- Without the hybrid flags the PR matches upstream: same speed, and the generated text is identical character for character (checked on both models).
- Run-to-run noise on the non-hybrid configs was up to ~5 t/s between rounds; the two hybrid rounds on the 35B model agreed within 3%.
- Prompt processing is not changed by the hybrid mode (~30-50 t/s in every config).
- Hybrid output drifts from the other configs after a few dozen tokens, as upstream's own configs do from each other when experts run through different CPU/GPU kernels. Each config is deterministic. `test-llama-archs` checks the hybrid configs against the CPU (NMSE <= 1e-4): 396/396 pass on CUDA (RTX 4060 Laptop and L4).

### Qwen3.5-35B-A3B IQ4_XS on a second machine (2 rounds)

**Hardware:** NVIDIA L4 (24 GB) on Google Colab, 12 vCPUs, 53 GB RAM.
**Builds:** upstream = ggml-org/llama.cpp master `d454a20`; PR = `3d37f74` (this branch merged with `d454a20`).
**Setup:** same prompt and flags as above, `--moe-cache-mib 5000` to approximate a 12 GB card.

| Build | Flags | Round 1 t/s | Round 2 t/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| upstream | (none; `-fit` chooses the offload) | 93.5 | 93.3 |
| upstream | `-ngl 99 --cpu-moe` | 31.4 | 31.4 |
| upstream | `-ngl 99 --cpu-moe --moe-cache-mib 5000` | 33.2 | 33.2 |
| PR | `-ngl 99 --cpu-moe --moe-cache-mib 5000` | 33.3 | 33.2 |
| **PR** | `... --moe-cache-hybrid --moe-cache-adaptive` | **41.3** | **41.6** |

- This 18.7 GB model fits entirely in the L4's 24 GB, so upstream's `-fit` row keeps every expert on the GPU and is the fastest; it is listed for completeness only. The hybrid mode is for models that do not fit in VRAM. Against the configs that keep the experts in host RAM, hybrid-adaptive is about 1.25x here (1.7x on the laptop above, where the CPU share is larger).

### Faster fill of the adaptive cache (`1967019`)

The adaptive cache used to fill its free slots at 16 experts per generated token, so a large cache took hundreds of tokens to fill and the hybrid ran behind upstream's cache until then. It now uploads the experts that missed right after the token that missed them (up to 512 per token, only while the cache has free slots). The swaps once the cache is full are unchanged.

L4 24 GB, same prompt as above; upstream = master `84746c5`, before = `4f025fa`, after = `1967019`. Generation t/s:

| Model, cache | Tokens | upstream cache | PR hybrid before | PR hybrid after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-Coder-Next UD-IQ4_XS (36 GB), 16 GB | 256 | 38.5 | 21.1 | **29.1** |
| | 1024 | 46.6 | 32.7 | **42.6** |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q6_K (27 GB), 16 GB | 256 | 37.8 | 32.4† | **34.3**‡ |
| | 1024 | 50.5 | 47.0 | **50.1**‡ |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B IQ4_XS, 5000 MiB | 256 | 33.5 | 41.4† | **45.9** |

† on the earlier head `3d37f74`. ‡ with the change one small edit before `1967019` (the periodic swap round now also runs while the cache fills).

- Generation t/s leaves out prompt processing, during which upstream's cache does its own loading (1.5-1.8 s here). In total time the hybrid matches upstream's cache on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B Q6_K: 21.4 s against 21.8 s for 1024 tokens.
- On Qwen3-Coder-Next (512 experts per layer) the hybrid still takes about 2 s longer at the start, while it uploads the experts after the prompt; over tokens 257-1024 both run at about 50 t/s.
- RTX 4060 Laptop, 4 GB cache, old and new code alternated: 40-42 vs 42-43 t/s at 256 tokens, 46-47 at 1024 for both.
- Accuracy is unchanged: L4 IQ4_XS, 20 chunks, hybrid + adaptive mean KLD 0.0040, max 0.13; `test-llama-archs` 402/402 on the L4.

### Accuracy (KL divergence)

`llama-perplexity --kl-divergence`, `-ub 1` so every token takes the hybrid path, 20 chunks of 512 tokens (the repo's docs). The base is the same build with `-ngl 99 --cpu-moe` and no cache.

| Machine and model | Config | Mean KLD | Max KLD | 99.9% KLD | Same top token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 4060 Laptop, Q6_K, 2048 MiB cache | cache | 0.00387 | 0.107 | 0.077 | 97.12% |
| | hybrid + adaptive | 0.00380 | 0.113 | 0.086 | 97.22% |
| L4, IQ4_XS, 5000 MiB cache | cache | 0.00411 | 0.166 | 0.070 | 97.20% |
| | hybrid + adaptive | 0.00388 | 0.241 | 0.074 | 97.20% |

Both configs differ from the base by the same small amount, which comes from running experts on GPU kernels instead of CPU kernels; the hybrid mode adds no divergence of its own on these runs.

### Known limitation

- The hybrid path is only used for 1-token batches. MTP and other speculative decoding verify several tokens per batch, so they currently do not benefit from it, and with the hybrid flags they can run slower than with the plain cache.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - Assisted in formatting CLI argument parsing and test fixtures; all kernel logic and cache architectures have been reviewed, tested, and validated locally across test-llama-archs.

items.title: Eval bug: Laguna repeats <assistant> on Metal for ubatches >= 32 tokens (ffn_moe_down input exceeds F16 range)
items.body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 0.7.0-dev (build 11669, commit 620d2225c)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000334 for Darwin arm64
```

The `build_moe_ffn` code involved is unchanged on master as of 2026-10-20.

### Operating systems

Mac (macOS 26.7.1)

### GGML backends

Metal

### Hardware

Apple M4 Max, 64 GB

### Models

[poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-GGUF) Q4_K_M (arch `laguna`)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

On Metal, Laguna-XS-2.1 generates only a repeating `<assistant>` token (id 23) when the prompt is evaluated in a ubatch of 32 or more tokens. A ubatch of 31 or fewer, `--cpu-moe`, and CPU-only runs all give correct output.

```sh
llama-completion -m Laguna-XS-2.1-Q4_K_M.gguf -no-cnv --temp 0 -n 16 -c 4096 \
  -p $'<system>You are a helpful, conversationally-fluent assistant. Answer questions clearly and concisely, and think step by step before replying.</system>\n<user>Hi</user>\n<assistant><think>'
```

The prompt is 42 tokens.

| Run | Output |
| --- | --- |
| default, `-ub 32` | `<assistant><assistant><assistant>…` |
| `-ub 31` | `Okay, the user said "Hi". I need to respond appropriately. Let me` |
| `--cpu-moe` | correct (same as above) |
| `-ngl 0 --device none` | correct |

The 32-token threshold matches `ggml_metal_op_mul_mat_id_use_mm` (`ne21 >= 32`). At that size the `mul_mm_id` kernel stages src1 in half precision.

Since #29029 (0f8a414b7), the src1 rescale in that kernel runs only when `GGML_PREC_F32` is set on src1. `build_moe_ffn` sets it only for `LLM_ARCH_MISTRAL4 || LLM_ARCH_MELLUM` (#30584, the fix for the same symptom in #30579).

Laguna's `ffn_moe_down` input also exceeds F16 range. A `-ngl` sweep fits accumulated overflow across layers rather than a single bad layer: `-ngl 2` is correct, while `-ngl 3` and higher loop.

**Fix, verified locally:** in `src/llama-graph.cpp` `build_moe_ffn`, add `|| arch == LLM_ARCH_LAGUNA` to that condition. With this change, Metal output at the default ubatch matches CPU.

### First Bad Commit

Probably 0f8a414b7 (#29029), which made the rescale opt-in. Not bisected.

### Relevant log output

No crash or error is logged; the output is wrong as shown in the table above.

items.title: llama : enable moe amax rescaling for laguna
items.body:
## Overview

Adds `LLM_ARCH_LAGUNA` to the existing `build_amax_src1_f16` condition in `build_moe_ffn`, so Laguna applies the same f16 activation rescaling already used by Mistral4, Mellum and Flint.

Without it, Laguna MoE models overflow on Metal when the prefill microbatch is 32 tokens or larger (#30896): `kernel_mul_mm_id` stages the f32 activation through `half` in shared memory, so gate/up outputs above 65504 become inf in the down projection. At smaller microbatches a different kernel path is used, which is why the failure only appears at ubatch >= 32.

Verified locally on a Laguna-XS-2.1 slice: the src1 amax into `ffn_moe_down` dropped from 103671.5 to 1018.9 with this change, and the unflagged Metal `MUL_MAT_ID` path produces NaN for src1 ~1e5 at n >= 32 while CPU does not.

## Additional information

Ref: #30896, #30584

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - an AI agent (Devin) located the bug mechanism, wrote the one-line change and the local verification probes; the patch follows the existing pattern from #30584.

items.title: Eval bug: Mellum 8x slower on CUDA since #30584 (ffn_moe_down MUL_MAT_ID falls back to CPU)
items.body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 0.7.0-dev (build 11682, commit f12aaa344)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64
```

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 6 GB (compute capability 8.6), 16 GB RAM, CUDA 13.0

### Models

https://huggingface.co/JetBrains/Mellum2.1-12B-A2.5B-Thinking-GGUF (commit `20b4394`), `MXFP4_MOE` and `Q4_K_M`

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Since #30584, Mellum is about 8x slower on CUDA. #30584 sets `GGML_PREC_F32` on src1 of `ffn_moe_down`, and the CUDA
`supports_op` rejects any `MUL_MAT_ID` with that flag (`ggml-cuda.cu:5501` at `f12aaa3`), so the down projection of
every layer runs on the CPU. This is the CUDA side of what #30544 describes for Vulkan with Mistral 4 (#29029).

```sh
llama-bench -m Mellum2.1-12B-A2.5B-Thinking-MXFP4_MOE.gguf -ngl 99 -ncmoe 13 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa 1 \
  -b 2048 -ub 1024 -p 512,4096 -n 128 -r 3
```

Same machine, ABA order (t/s):

| build | pp512 | pp4096 | tg128 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| b11580 (`4413a19`, before #30584) | 756 | 1165 | 44.7 |
| b11682 (`f12aaa3`) | 158 | 171 | 5.5 |
| b11580 (`4413a19`) | 754 | 1158 | 44.9 |
| b11682 with only the #30584 line reverted | 751 | 1157 | 45.2 |

Simply dropping the check in `supports_op` is not enough: batched MMQ aborts with
`mmq.cu:126: GGML_ASSERT(prec == GGML_PREC_UNDEFINED || prec == GGML_PREC_Q8 || prec == GGML_PREC_Q4) failed`.

With that check removed, I added `test-backend-ops` cases with Mellum's `ffn_moe_down` shape (64 experts, 8 used,
k=896, m=2304) and amax 1e5 / 3e5 to see which types the MMVQ path (n <= 8) handles:

| type_a | n=1 | n=4 |
|---|---|---|
| q8_0 | OK | OK |
| mxfp4 | OK | OK |
| iq4_nl | OK | OK |
| q4_K (k=2048, m=4096, 128 experts, 4 used) | OK | OK |
| q4_0 | NaN | NaN |
| q5_0 | NaN | NaN |

(n=8 with q8_0 is OK; n=8 with mxfp4 goes to MMQ and hits the assert above.)

Perplexity on the prompt from #30579 (`-c 2048 -b 2048 -ub 1`, all through MMVQ) with the check removed is finite and
close to CPU:

| quant | CUDA, -ub 1 | CPU (b11588) |
|---|---|---|
| Q4_K_M (`ffn_down_exps` is Q8_0) | 2.2399 2.2318 2.5135 | 2.2448 2.2385 2.5136 |
| MXFP4_MOE | 2.2720 2.2503 2.4692 | 2.2766 2.2508 2.4668 |

Before #30584, b11580 also gave finite perplexity with `-ub 512` on CUDA for both files (Q4_K_M 2.2360 2.2240 2.5079,
MXFP4_MOE 2.2787 2.2513 2.4559).

So for the official Mellum GGUFs, CUDA does not seem to need the CPU fallback in the MMVQ path. A fix along the lines of
#30544 (keep flagged `MUL_MAT_ID` on the GPU for mat-vec, at least for types without the q8_1 sum term) would recover
token generation; prompt processing would still fall back to the CPU unless MMQ supports the flag.

Tested only on this GPU. I have not checked other CUDA architectures or the `-ub 512` MMQ path with the check removed
beyond the assert.

### First Bad Commit

`5e03a1ff4` (#30584), confirmed by reverting only its one-line change on top of `f12aaa3`.

### Relevant log output

```console
ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmq.cu:126: GGML_ASSERT(prec == GGML_PREC_UNDEFINED || prec == GGML_PREC_Q8 || prec == GGML_PREC_Q4) failed
```

items.title: LLama-wackMall-fusion expert cache.

labels.name: ggml
labels.description: changes relating to the ggml tensor library for machine learning

items.body:
## Overview

This is expert caching combining ideas from several different prs to combine into my interpretation of the best of all worlds in stability, performance, user friendliness, and **maintainability**
The diff is at the size i think where its still acceptable unlike my early attempts, and it has resolved all issues anyone has had

Full (extensive*) credits table

## Attribution table:
| What | From |
|---|---|
| Running host-resident MoE experts on the GPU from a device cache: LRU with miss-only uploads, small-batch gate (32 tokens), separate banks per expert layout | [qvac-fabric](https://github.com/tetherto/qvac-fabric-llm.cpp), via https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887 (am17an) |
| Scheduler integration (routed ids read back and remapped, one upload shared by gate/up/down), cache disabled for the draft context, `--fit` accounting for the cache | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887 (am17an) |
| `--moe-cache-layers N` mirroring `--n-cpu-moe`, host experts placed through tensor overrides | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/15077, https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/11397 (slaren) |
| Staging uploads that copy only the used experts, merged into runs | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/15346 (slaren) |
| Fused `gate_up` expert tensors | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/20416 (ddh0) |
| Releasing only whole pages, `MADV_DONTNEED` rounded inward to page boundaries | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26003 (pwilkin) |
| Eviction that weighs use frequency instead of plain LRU | pashko-k (in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29887), https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/21609 (e1n00r) |
| Sizing the cache from free VRAM next to `--n-cpu-moe` | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/21614 (e1n00r) |
| Synchronizing before evicted experts are retired | pwasiewi (in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27861) |
| Distinct ids per token in `MUL_MAT_ID`, no shared dummy slot | Inovello (in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27861) |
| Hit/miss counters | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24524 (leloch) |
| Big batches kept off the cache, lessons from staging-tensor residency | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/23170 (avifenesh), https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/24524 (leloch) |
| Move mode aimed at mmap, measured against plain mmap with the page cache | pwilkin (in https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28414) |
| The host buffer types move mode has to handle (mapped, pinned `CUDA_Host`, plain) | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28223 (Inovello), https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26659 (bluechiperic) |
| Releasing the host pages of cached experts rather than pinning hot ones | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26414 (Ghimli), https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28545 (aryan0078) |
| Routing traces showing experts are reused enough to cache | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28544 (aryan0078) |
| The big-batch op offload path the staging planes plug into | https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/13386 (hjc4869), https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/18535 (DocShotgun) |

The first attempt:
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/26563

*Some of those are already merged. I still gave credits if I felt my ideas took from them

Original code to wackMall:
- Routing heatmap: per-expert usage tracked with decay, plus the heat log; admission and eviction governed by hysteresis, dwell, a sync period and a no-evict mode.
- Heat-weighted eviction order for the device cache.
- Move mode's release gate: host pages are released only once an expert has stayed cached long enough and sits clear of the coldest quarter, with rate-limited background read-back of released experts that turn cold.
- Copy mode by default; move mode runs only on mmap and falls back to copy.
- The --moe-cache-layers N|auto option, auto resolved through --fit.

## Performance

Generation speed (TG, tokens/s), single prompt, temperature 0, RTX 3070 Laptop (8 GB VRAM) + 32 GB RAM.
Stock = cache off; Cache on = `--moe-cache-layers auto`.

| Model | Stock | Cache on | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| LFM2.5-8B-A1B Q4_K_M | 238.2 | 242.8 | 1.02× |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B IQ2_M | 35.0 | 82.2 | 2.35× |
| Gemma-4-26B-A4B Q5_K_S | 15.0 | 46.0 | 3.06× |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6 | 13.0 | 24.7 | 1.90× |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B IQ2_M | 5.4 | 13.7 | 2.56× |

## Usage
--moe-cache-layers auto OR N
N is how many MoE layers get a GPU cache for their experts (--moe-cache-layers 8 = the experts of 8 layers). auto sizes it from the free VRAM. Default is 0 = off, everything as stock. Only affects models whose experts stay in host memory.

## Requirements

<!-- IMPORTANT: Please do NOT delete this section, otherwise your PR may be rejected -->

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md): Yes
- AI usage disclosure: Yes
